scene-u01-pnew1-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew1-3.text: Week 4 · KP05 Overfitting, underfitting and generalization

scene-u01-pnew1-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew1-5.text: Same 12 points, three complexities: a line can't bend, degree 2 is right, degree 9 threads the noise too

scene-u01-pnew1-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew1-6.text: How to read: each panel is one polynomial degree; solid blue dots are training points, hollow teal dots are unseen test points, the dark gray dashes are the true function.

scene-u01-pnew1-139.name: text#139
scene-u01-pnew1-139.text: Training is ten times below the floor

scene-u01-pnew1-140.name: text#140
scene-u01-pnew1-140.text: Source: idl-2026-fall lectures/lec04-kp05-overfitting-underfitting-generalization.md §1, caption fits (lecture's program, noise seed 11)

scene-u01-pnew2-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew2-3.text: Week 4 · KP05 Overfitting, underfitting and generalization

scene-u01-pnew2-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew2-5.text: Training error falls steadily with complexity; test error is lowest at $d=2$, then climbs

scene-u01-pnew2-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew2-6.text: How to read: blue is training MSE, teal is test MSE (log vertical axis); gray dashes are the noise floor $\sigma^2=0.09$; the gap between the lines keeps widening.

scene-u01-pnew2-66.name: text#66
scene-u01-pnew2-66.text: Green dot: lowest test MSE at $d=2$ ($0.0963$); $d=10$: test $0.440$, training $0.0069$ (lecture's program)

scene-u01-pnew2-69.name: text#69
scene-u01-pnew2-69.text: Higher degrees include lower ones; least squares only shrinks [Added]

scene-u01-pnew2-71.name: text#71
scene-u01-pnew2-71.text: ② Test MSE is lowest at $d=2$

scene-u01-pnew2-72.name: text#72
scene-u01-pnew2-72.text: $d=9$ is as bad as the line; $d=10$ is $4.9$ times the floor

scene-u01-pnew2-74.name: text#74
scene-u01-pnew2-74.text: ③ Test MSE always stays above the floor

scene-u01-pnew2-77.name: text#77
scene-u01-pnew2-77.text: ④ Training MSE below the floor is a warning

scene-u01-pnew2-78.name: text#78
scene-u01-pnew2-78.text: Below the floor from $d=2$ on: it starts memorizing noise

scene-u01-pnew3-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew3-3.text: Week 4 · KP05 Overfitting, underfitting and generalization

scene-u01-pnew3-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew3-5.text: Read the chart with bias and variance: underfitting is bias-driven, overfitting variance-driven

scene-u01-pnew3-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew3-6.text: How to read: each bar is the expected test MSE (averaged over 2000 redraws of training noise), split into squared bias, variance and noise floor, same scale.

scene-u01-pnew3-26.name: text#26
scene-u01-pnew3-26.text: One more parameter, a bit more variance (var $0.0250$)

scene-u01-pnew3-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew3-41.text: $\text{bias}^2$ $0.208$ is two thirds of the total;

scene-u01-pnew3-42.name: text#42
scene-u01-pnew3-42.text: wrong in the same place whatever the data

scene-u01-pnew3-45.name: text#45
scene-u01-pnew3-45.text: var is about $6$ times that of $d=2$;

scene-u01-pnew3-46.name: text#46
scene-u01-pnew3-46.text: new noise, a whole new curve

scene-u01-pnew3-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew3-49.text: This averages over all training sets: $d=9$ gives

scene-u01-pnew3-50.name: text#50
scene-u01-pnew3-50.text: $0.207$, not the $0.289$ of Figure 2's single set

scene-u01-pnew3-51.name: text#51
scene-u01-pnew3-51.text: Source: idl-2026-fall lectures/lec04-kp05-overfitting-underfitting-generalization.md §3 ($0.0000$ is $0$ within simulation error; lecture's program)

scene-u01-pnew4-3.name: text#3
scene-u01-pnew4-3.text: Week 4 · KP05 Overfitting, underfitting and generalization

scene-u01-pnew4-5.name: text#5
scene-u01-pnew4-5.text: Choose models by error on unseen data: look at training error and its gap to validation error

scene-u01-pnew4-6.name: text#6
scene-u01-pnew4-6.text: How to read: left, judge the state from two numbers, top to bottom; right, the cost of choosing by training error, what to do on a tie, and the question left for KP06.

scene-u01-pnew4-9.name: text#9
scene-u01-pnew4-9.text: Training error, validation error and the gap

scene-u01-pnew4-16.name: text#16
scene-u01-pnew4-16.text: Training very low, validation much higher

scene-u01-pnew4-28.name: text#28
scene-u01-pnew4-28.text: ✗ Low training error means a good model

scene-u01-pnew4-29.name: text#29
scene-u01-pnew4-29.text: ✗ Overfitting is caused by noise in the data

scene-u01-pnew4-31.name: text#31
scene-u01-pnew4-31.text: ✗ A complex enough model can't underfit

scene-u01-pnew4-32.name: text#32
scene-u01-pnew4-32.text: (too little training or too much regularization)

scene-u01-pnew4-35.name: text#35
scene-u01-pnew4-35.text: Choose by training error → always the most complex

scene-u01-pnew4-37.name: text#37
scene-u01-pnew4-37.text: among the worst of all candidates

scene-u01-pnew4-41.name: text#41
scene-u01-pnew4-41.text: On a tie, pick the simpler [Added]

scene-u01-pnew4-43.name: text#43
scene-u01-pnew4-43.text: a gap of $0.0008$, far below random variation;

scene-u01-pnew4-44.name: text#44
scene-u01-pnew4-44.text: fewer parameters, less variance (a rule in KP07)

scene-u01-pnew4-47.name: text#47
scene-u01-pnew4-47.text: Choosing the degree needs unseen data;

scene-u01-pnew4-48.name: text#48
scene-u01-pnew4-48.text: choosing directly by the test set is cheating #2.

scene-u01-pnew4-49.name: text#49
scene-u01-pnew4-49.text: With only 12 points, how to be thrifty yet honest?
